thread:
maya (product): Heads-up: launching a new "Tiered Soft Limits" policy for hosted routes and an automatic spike-crediting flow. Goal: reduce surprise overages for bursty apps while preserving protection against abuse. Target rollout: 2026-04-05 14:00 UTC. Details below.
emily (finance): Summary of money stuff? how do credits show on invoices? :money_with_wings:
raj (billing): TL;DR: small automatic credits for transient spikes (<= 15% monthly usage delta and <= $75 per incident) will be applied automatically and appear as a new invoice line item called "policy-adjustment (auto-credit)". Anything above that escalates to manual review.
lucas (sre): Enforcement mechanics: soft limits are non-blocking throttles with signal-level headers. We'll add X-Rate-Remaining-Soft and X-Rate-Reset-Soft to responses. If customer exceeds soft limit persistently (3 consecutive windows), switch to hard throttle per existing rules.
ben (cto): Ops note: this must not open a path to amplification attacks. Rate signalling + per-customer real-time anomaly scoring before issuing credits. Keep default anomaly threshold conservative.
sofia (support): Need canned replies + triage doc. Also, can we offer one-click opt-out for enterprise customers who want strict limits?
maya (product): Yes: enterprise opt-out flag (billing/admin console) during rollout. For self-serve orgs we default to opt-in for the credit flow.
emily (finance): Accounting workflow: auto-credit events are zero-impact to revenue recognition until they exceed $500/account/month. We'll capture event metadata for audit: incident_id, rationale, computed_credit_amount. Finance ok with invoice line naming.
raj (billing): Operational rules:
- Auto-credit cap: $75 per spike incident, $250 total per 30-day period by default.
- Startup tier (free credits) gets separate 30-day waiver up to $350 — applied automatically for accounts < $500 spend/month.
- Any auto-credit that would cause a negative invoice will be converted to an account credit balance instead.
- Manual review if single incident >$75 OR monthly credit sum >$250 OR anomaly score >0.8.
lucas (sre): Rollout plan:
1) 14:00 UTC: enable soft-limit headers + telemetry in canary (us-east-1-canary)
2) 14:30: enable auto-credit engine in read-only (audit-only) mode for 2 hours
3) 16:30: enable auto-credit live for 10% traffic
4) 17:30: global ramp to 100% over 2 hours if no safety triggers
Safety triggers: elevated error rate >0.4% OR anomalous credit rate >0.5% of accounts -> pause and revert to audit-only.
sofia (support): Customer message draft: "We're introducing tiered soft-limits and an automatic spike-crediting program to reduce unexpected overage charges for short bursts. Enterprise customers can opt out. You'll see any credit applied on your invoice under 'policy-adjustment (auto-credit)'." Feedback?
emily (finance): Add explicit guarantee: customers won't be double-billed — if we credit then later bill the same usage in error, we'll correct and notify within 48h. Also add contact for urgent billing disputes.
raj (billing): Dashboard: Billing -> SoftLimitCredits shows incident list, auto-credit amounts, account opt-out state, and manual review queue. Link: https://redwood.internal/billing/soft-limits-dashboard
ben (cto): Two asks: 1) telemetry retention for all soft-limit events = 120 days; 2) a fast-kill switch we can trigger from control plane (no deploy).
lucas (sre): Implementing kill-switch and extra retention. Also adding sampling of raw request footprints (sample rate 0.01) for forensics; PII scrub will run before storage.
maya (product): Internal runbook & FAQ: https://redwood.internal/docs/soft-limits-auto-credit. I'll post canned support replies there by EOD.
sofia (support): We'll staff 14:00-20:00 UTC rotation for tomorrow. Please ping #support-alerts at each stage.
billing-bot: scheduled: soft-limits-service v1.2.0 -> us-east-1-canary at 2026-04-05T14:00:00Z. Events to emit: canary-enabled, audit-mode-live, credits-live-10pct, global-ramp-started, credits-paused.
emily (finance): Can we temporarily suspend automatic charge attempts for accounts receiving auto-credit adjustments during the rollout window? Helps avoid customers getting charged and then credited immediately.
raj (billing): Good call. We'll set payment-attempt-suppression for accounts flagged by the auto-credit engine for 48h. Finance approved.
ben (cto): Keep the manual-review bar high; most automatic credits should be non-op. If we see exploitation patterns, we'll tighten thresholds.
maya (product): Thanks all. Final note: external communication will go out only after first 24h of stable metrics. Internal docs are canonical. I'll update this thread with status messages during rollout.
sofia (support): A reminder: include escalation contacts for enterprise accounts in the support doc.
maya (product): A tiny config snippet for ops team (example):
```
soft_limit:
  window_seconds: 60
  soft_percentile: 95
  auto_credit:
    enabled: true
    per_incident_cap: 75
    monthly_cap: 250
    startup_tier_cap: 350
```
lucas (sre): Logged. We'll monitor the 'credit-apply-rate' metric and post to #sre-alerts.
maya (product): OK everyone, thanks — let's keep conservative defaults and avoid surprises.
